_note: Landing copy for category pages, keyed by practice slug. Written to the term's landing_intro field by Categories\sync(), and only when that field is empty — anything typed in wp-admin is somebody's own writing and outranks this. Ten categories already had copy before this file existed and are deliberately absent from it. The voice follows the existing pages: open with the thing a visitor would not know, explain how the formats differ, then the practicalities, then a Related line. No claim that anything treats or cures a condition, and the categories that sit closest to health carry the same disclaimer the Community page does.

intros.mind:
Three quite different things share this shelf, and timetables rarely say which one you are booking.

Meditation classes are usually guided sittings — someone talks, you sit, it lasts half an hour to an hour. Mindfulness is more often taught as a course over six or eight weeks with the same group each time, and the practice is homework between sessions rather than the session itself. Breathwork is the physically demanding one: sustained patterned breathing that can leave your hands tingling and your emotions closer to the surface than you expected. Counselling and coaching are one-to-one and booked like an appointment.

On practicalities: several Perth sittings are free or by donation, and those tend to be the volunteer-run ones rather than the studios. Courses ask you to commit to the whole run and usually cost less per session than dropping in. Breathwork facilitators generally ask about pregnancy, heart conditions and epilepsy before a first session, so expect that question and answer it honestly.

Related: meditation classes, mindfulness coaching, breathwork, counselling, and yoga and movement.

Oria Haven is a directory, not a health service. If you have a health concern, speak with your GP or a registered practitioner.
intros.spa:
Recovery rooms sell time rather than treatments, and the price on the board is usually for the slot, not the thing you do in it.

The sessions differ more than the marketing suggests. A sauna is a long warm sit you can talk through; an ice bath is two or three minutes and you will not want to talk. Contrast therapy alternates the two and takes about an hour with the changing. Float tanks are an hour on your own in dark salt water, which some people find restful and others find far too quiet. Infrared saunas run cooler than traditional ones and feel less punishing, and sound baths belong here too — you lie down, someone plays bowls and gongs, and nothing is required of you.

On practicalities: most studios sell memberships that only make sense if you go weekly, and casual rates are the honest way to find out whether you will. Bring or hire a towel, allow twenty minutes on top of the session for changing and showering, and book contrast in the middle of the day if you would rather not drive home cold.

Related: infrared sauna, ice baths, contrast therapy, float therapy, sound healing, and red light therapy.
intros.experiences:
A day retreat and a bushwalk are both on this page, and the difference between them is mostly how much of your day is planned for you.

Day retreats run four to eight hours in one place, usually with food, and combine two or three of movement, sitting, sound and rest. Weekend retreats add accommodation and a second morning, which is where most of the value is. Guided walks and forest bathing sessions are shorter and cheaper and generally ask nothing of your fitness beyond being able to walk for an hour or two. Surf and ocean sessions are the ones with actual conditions attached, and they get moved.

On practicalities: retreats book out further ahead than anything else in the directory, and the small ones fill first because they are small. Read what is included before comparing prices — accommodation, meals and transfers move the number a long way. For anything outdoors in Perth, check the forecast and the fire danger rating the day before, and expect a change of plan in summer.

Related: wellness retreats, day retreats, forest bathing, bushwalking, surf sessions, and walking groups.
intros.beauty:
Salons and skin clinics are listed together here, and the title on the door tells you less than the qualification of the person treating you.

A beauty therapist covers facials, waxing, brows, lashes and nails. A dermal therapist or dermal clinician has additional training and works with the treatments that go deeper — peels, microneedling, LED and light-based work — usually after a consultation rather than a straight booking. Some clinics are doctor-led and offer prescription treatments; those are a different kind of appointment and are not listed as services here.

On practicalities: first appointments at a skin clinic are often a consultation rather than a treatment, and paying for one is normal. Patch tests are standard before tinting, lash work and some peels, and a salon that insists on one is doing its job. Courses of treatments are usually sold at a discount, so be reasonably sure of the practitioner before committing to six.

Related: facials, skin treatments, lashes and brows, nails, and waxing.
intros.longevity:
This is the newest corner of Perth wellness and the least standardised, which shows in what things cost.

Most of what sits here is measurement plus a protocol — testing of some kind, then a plan built on it — combined with the recovery equipment that turns up in the Spa and Recovery pages as well. Sauna, cold exposure, red light and compression appear in both places because the same studios sell them to two different audiences. What is particular to this page is the tracking: baseline testing, repeat testing, and someone reading the results with you.

On practicalities: ask what is actually measured and how often before paying for a package, and ask what happens to the data afterwards. Prices vary more here than anywhere else in the directory for what looks like the same session, so it is worth ringing two places.

Related: red light therapy, ice baths, infrared sauna, compression therapy, and exercise physiology.
